result:
Three tests fail for reasons other than the `partitioned` keyword problem. One more (the flaky one) is probably a side effect of it.

1. **`tests/test_helpers.py::TestStreaming::test_async_view`** fails because the optional async dependency is not installed. `Tessel.ensure_sync` (`src/tessel/app.py:1096`) raises `RuntimeError: Install Tessel with the 'async' extra in order to use async views`. This is an environment gap, separate from the Werkzeug version.

2. **`tests/test_request.py::test_limit_config`** fails an assertion: `Request({}).max_form_memory_size` is `None` instead of `500_000` outside an app context. `src/tessel/wrappers.py:111` falls back to `super().max_form_memory_size`, and Werkzeug 3.0.3 has no non-`None` default for it. It is still caused by the old Werkzeug (3.0.3 vs the required `>=3.1.0`), but through a different missing feature than `partitioned`. If you group strictly by mechanism, it is separate from the session-cookie failures.

3. **`tests/test_helpers.py::test_open_resource_exceptions[a]`** failed in the first full run only. It passes in isolation and in later full runs, so it is flaky. The likely cause is the `stream_with_context` generator leaked by `test_stream_keeps_session`, which is garbage-collected and emits an "unraisable exception" warning attributed to a later test. I did not capture its original traceback, so this attribution is an inference.

The teardown ERROR on `test_stream_keeps_session` (`assert not leaks`, `tests/conftest.py:79`) is a knock-on of the `partitioned` `TypeError`. The request died mid-stream and left the app context unpopped, so it belongs to the main cause.

That leaves 19 failures from the `partitioned` problem plus the one teardown error, and the three tests above.

_cmd.prompt: Which of the failing tests are NOT caused by that main root cause? Name them and say briefly why each fails.
